chapters.title: Motivation
chapters.sourcePressure: Robert Philippe can still understand his life after returning from South America, but his initiative collapses; the chapter connects that launch failure to locus of control, Marine boot camp, nursing-home rebellions, and a bias toward action.
chapters.coreMove: Turn a stalled obligation into a self-authored next move that the actor can choose and start.
chapters.commonMisread: Motivation means wanting the outcome badly enough.

chapters.title: Teams
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter centers on psychological safety: Google data scientists studied teams for four years and found that interaction quality matters more than individual composition; Saturday Night Live supplies a creative-room echo.
chapters.coreMove: Diagnose the room by how safely useful signal moves before status fear edits it out.
chapters.commonMisread: Good teams are just groups with the strongest people.

chapters.title: Focus
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter ties focus to cognitive tunneling, Air France Flight 447, and the power of mental models; it treats narrowed pressure-attention as the danger and prebuilt models as the corrective.
chapters.coreMove: Use a mental model to keep scanning for context when pressure tries to shrink attention to one cue.
chapters.commonMisread: Focus means blocking everything out and staring harder.

chapters.title: Goal Setting
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter uses SMART goals, stretch goals, and the Yom Kippur War to show that targets shape action, ambition, and strategic judgment, sometimes helpfully and sometimes dangerously.
chapters.coreMove: Pair specific targets with stretch and reality checks so the metric steers the mission without replacing it.
chapters.commonMisread: Goals work when they are either precise or inspiring.

chapters.title: Managing Others
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter's subtitle anchors managing others in solving a kidnapping with lean and agile thinking and a culture of trust, pointing to adaptive coordination under uncertainty.
chapters.coreMove: Build trust-rich feedback loops that let reality change the plan before control hardens into blindness.
chapters.commonMisread: Managing others means telling people what to do more clearly.

chapters.title: Decision Making
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter connects forecasting the future, poker, and Bayesian psychology to decisions under hidden information, probability, and belief-updating.
chapters.coreMove: Make the best current bet while keeping uncertainty visible enough to update when evidence changes.
chapters.commonMisread: Decision making means picking the option that feels most certain.

chapters.title: Innovation
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter uses idea brokers, creative desperation, and Disney's Frozen to argue that innovation is transfer plus hard revision, not isolated originality.
chapters.coreMove: Import useful patterns from elsewhere, recombine them under pressure, and cut until the new fit is real.
chapters.commonMisread: Innovation means inventing something no one has seen before.

chapters.title: Absorbing Data
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter closes on turning information into knowledge in Cincinnati's public schools, making data absorption an interpretation and shared-understanding problem rather than a collection problem.
chapters.coreMove: Convert raw information into shared knowledge by filtering, framing, and deciding what the pattern changes next.
chapters.commonMisread: Data is useful once you have enough of it.
